Brazilian Amphibian Species List Dataset (2026)

Source: R/data.R
drummond2026.Rd

The 2026 edition of the official Brazilian Amphibian Species List published by the Brazilian Herpetological Society (SBH), by Drummond et al. (2026), with the national threat category of each species according to the Portaria MMA nº 1.704/2026.

Usage

drummond2026

Format

drummond2026

A data frame with 1,251 rows and 11 columns:

species_id

Id of species in list

order

Taxonomic Order

family

Taxonomic Family

subfamily

Taxonomic Subfamily

tribe

Taxonomic Tribe (Hylidae only)

genus

Genus

epithet

Specific epithet

species

Scientific name

author

Authorship of original description

status

Change relative to Segalla et al. (2021), see details

category

Threat category by Portaria MMA 1.704/2026, see details

Source

https://zenodo.org/records/18340087 (CC BY 4.0) and https://www.in.gov.br/en/web/dou/-/portaria-mma-n-1.704-de-16-de-junho-de-2026-712968917

Details

The list includes 1,206 Anura, 40 Gymnophiona and 5 Caudata species (125 genera, 28 families), with records in Brazil up to 12 March 2026. Compared to Segalla et al. (2021), 41 species were removed and 104 were added. The status column records the change for each species: "recently described species" (75 species described since 2021), "taxonomic change or new record" (29 species added by revalidation, removal from synonymy or new records in Brazil) and "new combination" (63 species moved to another genus, such as Scinax to Ololygon and Julianus, or Lysapsus to Pseudis). The full list of changes, including the removed species, is in data-raw/mudancas_2021_2026.csv in the package source.

In Hylidae, the subfamily is Hylinae and the tribes (Cophomantini, Dendropsophini, ...) are in tribe. In segalla2021 these groups are in the subfamily column.

category follows Annex I (CR, EN, VU, "CR (PE)" = possibly extinct) and Annex II (EX = extinct) of the Portaria MMA nº 1.704, de 16 de junho de 2026 (DOU 17/06/2026). The Portaria lists only threatened and extinct species, so NA means the species is not on those lists (it includes LC, NT and DD species and species not yet assessed). Names are matched exactly; the Portaria also lists Bokermannohyla napolii (VU), now a junior synonym of B. ravida, and that category is not transferred.

References

Drummond, L.O., Santana, D.J., Lima, A.P. & Toledo, L.F. (2026). List of Amphibians of Brazil. Herpetologia Brasileira, 15(2). doi:10.5281/zenodo.18340087
